transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-21 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Camila Rivera (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood CSM); Alex Kim (Seabright CISO), Marta Lopez (Dir Eng), Ethan Price (Cloud Architect)

Summary:
High-level security discovery for Seabright Health evaluating Redwood for a mix of hosted and private deployments. Key concerns: SOC 2/ISO compliance, SSO/SAML and IdP integration, RBAC and least-privilege, audit logs and retention, encryption (KMS/HSM), and data residency/data retention policies. Customer wants clear artifact delivery (reports, architecture), and an on-prem/VPC design for regulated PHI workloads.

Topics:
- Compliance posture (SOC 2 type II, ISO 27001)
- Authentication and SSO (SAML, SCIM provisioning)
- Authorization (RBAC, fine-grained roles, separation of duties)
- Logging and audit (immutable logs, retention, SIEM integration)
- Encryption and key management (KMS, HSM, BYOK)
- Data residency and retention policies
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros and then we can dig into the security items you flagged on the sign-up questionnaire.
[00:18] Alex: Hi, Alex here, CISO at Seabright. We run a lot of PHI workflows, so the security checklist was long. We're especially curious about where Redwood stores data for hosted, and what options exist for private deployments.
[00:34] Camila: Thanks Alex. Broadly we support hosted API for lower-risk workflows and Dedicated or Private (VPC/on-prem) when customers need isolation. For PHI we typically recommend Private/VPC with customer-managed network and optional on-prem packaging.
[00:52] Marta: Can you confirm Redwood has SOC 2 and ISO artifacts? We'll need those for our procurement and security review.
[01:05] Jordan: Yes - we have SOC 2 Type II and are certified to ISO 27001; I can share the reports under an NDA. We'll send both the attestation and summary controls.
[01:20] Alex: Great. Timing: we need the docs by end of week to get through our legal intake.
[01:27] Jordan: Noted. I'll get them over by Tuesday - is that okay?
[01:31] Alex: Perfect.
[01:35] Ethan: Next, SSO. Our IdP is Okta, and we provision via SCIM. How mature is Redwood's SSO and provisioning support?
[01:49] Camila: We support SAML2.0 for SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC is supported with role templates; you can map your IdP groups to Redwood roles. There are some edge cases around delegated admin vs full admin, we can walk through those.
[02:08] Marta: Do roles support least privilege? We want to ensure engineers can't access audit logs or KMS keys unless explicitly granted.
[02:18] Camila: Yes - roles are fairly granular (viewer, operator, admin, security-audit). We also have an Audit role that provides read-only access to logs without admin privileges. We'll send the role matrix.
[02:32] Alex: How are audit logs exported? We want immutable write-once logs and to forward to our SIEM (Splunk).
[02:44] Camila: We provide audit logs via S3 export, and we can stream logs to customer SIEM using a secure forwarder or push to your ingestion endpoint. Logs are timestamped and include user, action, resource, and request IDs. For private deployments logs can be kept entirely in your VPC.
[03:05] Ethan: What about tamper-resistance - can logs be write-once/read-many or integrated with an append-only store?
[03:13] Camila: For hosted, we maintain append-only logging with retention controls and cryptographic integrity checks; for Private, you manage storage and can use your WORM S3 buckets or an internal logging appliance.
[03:26] Jordan: Also we support configurable retention windows per account and per log type; we can match common regulatory retention policies.
[03:35] Alex: Encryption - do you support customer-managed keys? HSM?
[03:41] Camila: We support BYOK via KMS integration for Private and Dedicated. Hosted customers can use Redwood-managed KMS keys by default; for customers needing stronger controls we offer HSM-backed keys in Dedicated and Private, and integrations with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault.
[04:00] Ethan: If we use BYOK, are keys rotated automatically? Who has access to key material?
[04:07] Camila: Key rotation policies are configurable. With BYOK the customer controls rotation; Redwood never stores plaintext key material. Access to key material is restricted to the KMS; Redwood services request encryption/decryption via KMS APIs using minimal IAM roles. We'll provide the KMS integration diagram.
[04:26] Marta: Network controls: can we run the inference nodes in our VPC with no public egress?
[04:35] Camila: Yes - Private deployments can run entirely within your VPC with no public internet egress. Dedicated can be configured with VPC peering or private connectivity too.
[04:45] Alex: Are there SOC2 controls around change management and vulnerability scanning that we can review?
[04:53] Jordan: Yes, our SOC 2 includes change control, vulnerability management, and patch windows; Camila will pull out the specific control mappings.
[05:05] Ethan: Performance question: if we move to Private because of PHI, are there feature parity limitations vs hosted? For example, streaming, function calling, or model rollout controls?
[05:18] Camila: We maintain parity for core inference features, but some hosted-only telemetry features (multi-tenant usage analytics) are limited in Private by design. Model rollouts and canarying are supported in Private via the same control plane, depending on configuration. We'll highlight any known feature gaps in the architecture doc.
[05:40] Marta: Data residency - we have requirements for EU patient data to remain in-region. How do you handle region selection?
[05:50] Camila: You can pin deployments to specific regions. For hosted we have region selection for endpoints; for Private you deploy into the customer's region. We'll document region support and the regions where we have certified KMS/HSM support.
[06:06] Alex: One of our compliance reviewers asked about RBAC auditability - can we get a log of who granted which role to whom and when?
[06:16] Camila: Yes, every role change is recorded in the audit trail with actor, timestamp, and request ID. Those are exportable.
[06:26] Jordan: On the procurement side, pricing for Dedicated vs Private varies; we can outline the procurement template once you choose architecture.
[06:35] Ethan: Any known limitations for encryption-in-transit? We use mTLS internally.
[06:42] Camila: We support TLS1.2+ and can configure mutual TLS in Private deployments. Hosted endpoints use standard TLS and token-based auth; for higher assurance we can negotiate mTLS for dedicated/private connectivity.
[06:58] Marta: Incident response - how do you notify customers for breaches or incidents?
[07:04] Jordan: We have a documented incident response policy; we notify customers per SLA timelines, provide a post-incident report, and engage a joint incident review. We'll include the IR summary in the package.
[07:16] Alex: Do you offer penetration test reports or third-party security assessments?
[07:21] Camila: Yes, we have recent third-party pentest summaries and can provide redacted reports under NDA.
[07:30] Ethan: For the PoC, we want to run a small benchmark on our sample data. How fast can you spin up a dedicated pool for testing?
[07:38] Camila: For a PoC we can provision a small Dedicated pool in a week if capacity is available; Private on-prem takes longer - typically 3-6 weeks depending on network and provisioning.
[07:50] Marta: Cost tradeoffs - if we keep in hosted but want private data handling, what are the options?
[07:58] Jordan: You can use hosted for non-PHI and route PHI workloads to Dedicated/Private. We also support request routing policies so sensitive requests hit private endpoints and everything else uses hosted for lower cost.
[08:14] Alex: Perfect. Next steps and artifacts?
[08:18] Jordan: I'll send SOC2 and ISO summaries, Camila will share VPC and KMS integration diagrams, and we'll schedule a dedicated demo for the PoC with performance benchmarks.
[08:30] Samir: I'll own CSM coordination and make sure we have the right follow-up dates on the calendar.

Recap / Close:
[08:40] Jordan: Thanks all - we heard: 1) you need SOC2/ISO artifacts (Alex), 2) detailed VPC/KMS diagram and role matrix (Marta/Ethan), 3) PoC dedicated pool for benchmarking. We'll target sending docs by 2026-03-23 and reconvene the week of 2026-03-29 for the dedicated demo.
[08:58] Alex: Sounds good, thanks.
[09:02] Marta: Thanks everyone.

References mentioned:

End of transcript.
